title: Move jim.tennis onto the released image
description: Replace the current deploy (rsync source to the droplet, build on a small server, restart) with pulling a released image. This proves the upgrade path that other clubs will use, on real data, before anyone else depends on it. Steps: droplet snapshot; in-app backup; switch the compose file to the published image; start; verify; keep the previous image for rollback. Then retire scripts/deploy-app.sh's build path and rewrite the production runbook around 'pull version, restart'. This changes production and must be done with Jim present and only on his explicit go-ahead on the day.

recommended_model.name: Opus 5.5
recommended_model.rationale: A production change on real data; needs judgement and a careful rollback plan, with the owner present.

acceptance_criteria: Jim has given an explicit go-ahead on the day and a droplet snapshot was taken first
jim.tennis runs the published image at a named version; /version confirms it
All existing data, sessions policy, player links and push subscriptions work after the switch
Rollback to the previous image was rehearsed or the exact command is recorded and tested on a copy
docs/PRODUCTION_QUICK_REFERENCE.md describes the new procedure and the lessons from the switch
The droplet no longer needs the Go source tree or a build step for the app

notes: Production runs CourtHive alongside; this item touches only the app service.
Existing administrator accounts on jim.tennis are unaffected by WI-123.
After pulling a production database locally, recreate the container with `up -d`, not `start`, so .env is re-read.

testing_requirements: Smoke test checklist run against production after the switch

context.user_story: As the maintainer, I want my own club on the same release path as everyone else.
context.programme: Club-readiness programme (sprints 019-024). Agreed constraints: BHPLTA clubs only; each club self-hosts its own instance; the original author must have no access to any other club's instance (no seeded accounts, no shared or default secrets, no phone-home); passkeys are the default sign-in with passwords as an optional fallback; the captain role is real; SQLite is the only supported database; CourtHive is bundled as an opt-in part of the package so clubs can run their own club championships.
